item.title: In a fruit shop
item.description: Name different fruits and ask for the kind, size or amount you want to buy.

children.definition: A sweet fruit that is wide and round at the bottom and narrow at the top.
children.example: Can I have that big green pear, please?

children.definition: A round, sweet fruit with tiny, soft hairs on its skin and a large, hard stone inside.
children.example: I'd like one soft peach to eat today, please.

children.definition: A small fruit with smooth skin, often purple, and one hard stone inside.
children.example: Can I try a purple plum before I buy a kilo?

children.definition: Small, round fruits that grow close together and can be green, red or purple.
children.example: Can I have half a kilo of green grapes, please?

children.definition: A sweet red fruit with tiny seeds on the outside and small green leaves on top.
children.example: May I try a strawberry from this box?

children.definition: A very small, round fruit, often red or dark red, with one hard stone inside.
children.example: Can I taste a cherry before I buy a bag?

children.definition: A yellow fruit that tastes very sour and is often a little pointed at both ends.
children.example: I'll take one large lemon for my tea, please.

children.definition: A large, sweet fruit with thick skin and many seeds together in the middle.
children.example: Can I buy half a melon for tonight?

children.definition: A round, sweet fruit with bright skin the same color as a carrot and juicy pieces inside.
children.example: Can I have one big orange to make juice?

children.definition: A big fruit with hard, rough skin, long green leaves on top and sweet yellow fruit inside.
children.example: I'd like that whole pineapple, please.

children.definition: A long, curved fruit with soft, sweet fruit inside and skin that turns yellow when it is ready to eat.
children.example: Can I buy just one banana for my lunch?

children.definition: A small, round, pale orange fruit with fine, soft hairs on its skin and a hard, flat stone inside.
children.example: Can I try an apricot before I buy some for lunch?

children.definition: A small fruit with brown, hairy skin and usually green fruit inside with tiny black seeds.
children.example: Is this kiwi soft enough to eat today?

children.definition: A small, soft fruit with green or purple skin and many tiny seeds inside.
children.example: I'd like one fresh fig to try, please.
